fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeMnNi substitution study does not reconstruct the target CoCrFeNiTi powder-processing intervention involving high-energy ball milling and spark-plasma sintering.

Replacing Mn with W or Mo changes chemistry, elastic modulus, short-range order, stacking-fault energy, and precipitation tendency in addition to atomic-size mismatch, so the proposed comparison cannot uniquely attribute strengthening to lattice distortion.
No cited or existing evidence supports formation of the required single-phase FCC W- or Mo-substituted alloys or the predicted monotonic strength response.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible and testable as an alternative solid-solution-strengthening study. It defines a baseline, predicts increased hardness and yield strength, limits the claim to the single-phase FCC regime, and gives a reasonable falsification criterion. It nevertheless misses nearly all target-specific features: CoCrFeNiTi composition, milling and SPS parameters, nanocrystalline grain refinement, milling-induced dislocation density, FCC/BCC phase fractions, densification, and the quantitative hardness and compressive-strength outcomes. Its mechanism overlaps the target only through lattice-strain/solid-solution strengthening. Discriminability is limited because W or Mo substitution alters several strengthening-relevant variables simultaneously; matched grain size and dislocation density, direct solute-dislocation interaction measurements, and comparison against substitutions chosen to separate size from modulus or chemical effects would be needed to establish causal dominance.
